In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with a parton energy spectrum and FF modifications that are not inconsistent with QCD.

the parton fragmentation process has been significantly modified by interactions in nuclear collisions, and that the nature of the modification is consistent with parton color reconnections in the QCD vacuum and parton color deconfinement in a quark-gluon plasma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parton fragmentation is a key process that must be understood for the interpretation of nuclear collision data.

the observed nuclear modifications of partons and hadrons in $A$-$\overrightarrow{A}$ collisions are consistent with the hypothesis that partons are not thermalized and that parton energy loss is not the primary mechanism responsible for the observed nuclear modifications.

the observed parton energy-loss or medium-modification effects are consistent with a QCD-based picture of parton fragmentation, but are not consistent with a thermalization-based picture of partonic matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear collisions are more complicated than previously thought, and that the assumption of FF universality should be abandoned.

the observed suppression of the ${p}_{t}\ensuremath{\propto}1/\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ hard component in Au-Au collisions can be explained in the absence of parton thermal equilibrium by invoking parton ``medium modification'' in the form of altered parton fragmentation functions.
the observed parton energy loss is not due to parton-medium interactions, but rather is a manifestation of parton-medium interactions.
